obesity is a risk factor for the development of mood disorders, and that mood disorders can be a risk factor for obesity.

obesity is a risk factor for depression and anxiety, and that depression and anxiety are risk factors for obesity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found a high prevalence of obesity and mood disorder in the general population, that these conditions co-occur frequently and that the impact of obesity on mood disorders is not well understood.
we found no evidence that the use of the 3- and 5-item PHQ-9 is superior to the 9-item version in terms of validity and reliability.
we found that obesity and mood disorders are associated with increased risk for physical comorbidity, poorer psychological well-being, poorer health behaviours and increased use of health services.
